**Monthly Product Release · October 14, 2026**

This release includes four updates:

- [Clock-out confirmation, now available to all customers](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/en-us/articles/43859163908119-October-2026#clock-out-confirmation)

- [Create contact and Edit contact permissions](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/en-us/articles/43859163908119-October-2026#contact-permissions)

**■ New feature**

## Clock-out confirmation, now available to all customers

**Available in:** Web portal · TrackTik Guarding Application · TT-Shift · All customers

**Note:** Only available for Site Licenses and site schedules. Guards need a scheduled shift, and it isn’t available at zone level.

#### Release summary

**Affected modules**

Web portal — Clock-Out Confirmation Settings (Global, Region, Site); TrackTik Guarding Application and TT-Shift mobile apps; Daily Activity Report

**Note:** Only available for Site Licenses and site schedules. Guards need a scheduled shift, and it isn’t available at zone level.

**Customer action required**

No — automatic update. Clock-out confirmation stays off until an admin turns it on.

#### Overview

Clock-out confirmation is now available to every customer. Admins can turn it on and set it up themselves in the portal, without contacting Customer Success first. It’s off by default, so guards won’t see anything different until an admin turns it on.

**Who benefits most:** Operations managers and account admins who need a record of each guard acknowledging the end of their shift, for accountability, audits or compliance.

**What drove the change:** Clock-out confirmation first shipped in December 2025, but turning it on meant raising a request with Customer Success. That step is gone.

#### What's new

**What it does**

Guards acknowledge the end of their shift before they can clock out. Admins set it up in the portal:

- **Acknowledgment Method:** Signature capture (guard signs on screen before agreeing) or No confirmation required (no signature).
- **Agree or Disagree:** guards check the confirmation prompt, sign if a signature is required, then select Agree or Disagree. If they disagree, they’re asked for a reason, which shows on the Daily Activity Report.
- **Custom Text Prompt (Boilerplate):** the message guards read at clock-out, up to 500 characters. Leave it blank to use the default message.
- **Global, Region or Site level:** Site overrides Region, and Region overrides Global. For example, if a region requires a signature but one site is set to No confirmation required, guards at that site don’t sign.
- **In the mobile apps:** TrackTik Guarding Application and TT-Shift. Guards see the prompt when they select Clock Out, after any shift-end steps. Changes reach devices within 24 hours, when a guard starts a new shift or refreshes shift data.
- **In the Daily Activity Report:** a Clock-Out Confirmation section shows the confirmation text, the acknowledgment (Yes / No), the decline reason if there is one, and the signature.
- **Who can see it:** users need Scheduling enabled plus the View Clock Out Confirmation permission (under View Scheduling Reports). Without them, confirmation data stays hidden even when the feature is on.
- **Turned off (Require Confirmation set to No):** the mobile apps ignore all saved settings and guards see no prompt.

**Why it matters**

Customers get a recorded acknowledgement, signed if they want it, from each guard at the end of every shift. When a guard disagrees, the reason is on file. And any admin can now turn it on without waiting on a support request.

**How to access it**

Site level: open the site > **Settings** \> **Clock-Out Confirmation Settings**

The same settings are available at Region and Global level: **Settings** \> **General** \> **Clock-Out Confirmation Settings**

#### Rollout and upgrade

**Rollout method**

Automatic for all. The settings are available on every portal; the feature stays off until an admin enables it.

**Customer action required**

None — automatic. To turn it on (optional):

1. Open the site and go to **Settings** \> **Clock-Out Confirmation Settings**. (Region: **Settings** \> **General** \> **Clock-Out Confirmation Settings**)
2. Set **Require Confirmation** to **Yes**.
3. Choose the **Acknowledgment Method**.
4. Optional: enter a **Custom Text Prompt (Boilerplate)**, up to 500 characters. Leave it blank for the default message.
5. Select **Save**.

Guards’ devices pick up the change within 24 hours. To turn it off again, set Require Confirmation to No and select Save.

## Separate Create and Edit permissions for customers, positions and zones

**Available in:** Web portal · Admin Portal Roles · All customers

#### Release summary

**Affected modules**

Web portal — Settings > Roles & Security (Admin Portal Roles > Customer permission folder); Sites, Zones and Positions

**Customer action required**

No — automatic update. Existing roles keep the access they have today.

#### Overview

Admins can now let a role edit customers, positions and customer zones without also letting it create new ones. The three combined Create / Edit permissions in the Customer folder of Admin Portal Roles are now split into separate Create and Edit permissions. Existing roles keep exactly the access they have today.

**Who benefits most:** Account admins who manage roles, and organizations where managers or supervisors keep site and client records up to date but shouldn’t be setting up new ones.

**What drove the change:** Built in response to customer feedback. Managers who only needed to update existing records, like a site contact’s phone number or email, could also create sites because the permission bundled both. Sites were getting created that shouldn’t have been.

#### What's new

**What it does**

Three combined permissions in the Customer folder are now six separate ones:

- _Create / Edit a Customer_ **→** **Edit a Customer** and **Create a Customer**
- _Create / Edit Positions_ **→** **Edit Positions** and **Create Positions**
- _Create or Edit a Customer Zones_ **→** **Edit a Customer Zones** and **Create Customer Zones**

**How they work together**

- **Create includes Edit.** A role with Create can still edit existing records, even if Edit is unchecked.
- **Edit only:** users can open and edit existing sites, clients, positions and zones. Create options are hidden (for example Add Zone and Create a Position), and so are Duplicate and delete on positions.
- **Neither:** users can’t create or edit that record type. Whether zones are visible at all is still controlled by View Customer Zones.
- **Admin Portal Roles only.** Staff Portal Roles and Client Portal Roles don’t change.

**Why it matters**

Admins can match access to the job. People who maintain existing records, like updating a contact number or adjusting a position, no longer get the ability to create new sites, positions or zones. That means fewer incorrectly created records to clean up.

**How to access it**

**Settings** \> **Roles & Security** \> **Roles/Permissions** \> **Admin Portal Roles** \> \[select role\] > **Permission** \> **Customer**

#### Rollout and upgrade

**Rollout method**

Automatic for all

**Customer action required**

None — automatic. To make a role edit-only (optional):

1. Go to **Settings** \> **Roles & Security** \> **Roles/Permissions**.
2. Under **Admin Portal Roles**, select the role.
3. On the **Permission** tab, open the **Customer** folder.
4. Uncheck **Create a Customer**, **Create Positions** or **Create Customer Zones**, and keep the matching Edit permission checked.

Because Create includes Edit, unchecking only Edit doesn’t remove edit access.

## Create contact and Edit contact permissions

**Available in:** Web portal · Admin Portal Roles and Staff Portal Roles · Sites and Zones · All customers

#### Release summary

**Affected modules**

Web portal — Settings > Roles & Security (Admin Portal Roles and Staff Portal Roles > Customer folder); site Other Site Contacts / Addresses tab; zone Contacts tab

**Customer action required**

No — automatic update. Both permissions are on by default for every Admin and Staff Portal role, so access doesn’t change until an admin turns one off.

#### Overview

Admins can now control who adds and changes site and zone contacts. Two new permissions, Create contact and Edit contact, sit in the Customer folder for Admin Portal Roles and Staff Portal Roles. Both are on by default for every role, so nothing changes until an admin turns one off.

**Who benefits most:** Account admins who manage roles, and organizations where some staff need to look up site and zone contacts without adding or changing them.

**What drove the change:** Until now, site and zone contacts weren’t covered by a permission. Anyone who could open a site or zone could add and edit its contacts, and admins had no way to limit that.

#### What's new

**What it does**

Two new permissions in the **Customer** folder of **Admin Portal Roles** and **Staff Portal Roles** control who can add and change site and zone contacts:

- **Create contact:** shows the **Create Contact** button on a site’s **Other Site Contacts / Addresses** tab and on a zone’s **Contacts** tab. Without it, the button is hidden.
- **Edit contact:** lets users change existing site and zone contacts. Without it, they can still see contacts but can’t edit them.

**How they work together**

- **They work independently.** Create contact doesn’t include Edit contact, and Edit contact doesn’t include Create contact. A role that should do both needs both checked.
- **Same rule at site and zone level.** One pair of permissions covers contacts on sites and on zones.
- **On by default.** Every existing Admin and Staff Portal role gets both permissions turned on, so nobody loses access on release day.

**Why it matters**

Admins decide who maintains contact records. For example, let supervisors correct a contact’s phone number or email without letting them add new contacts, or make contacts read-only for roles that only need to look them up. Fewer unexpected changes to contact details other people rely on.

**How to access it**

Permissions: **Settings** \> **Roles & Security** \> **Roles/Permissions** \> **Admin Portal Roles** (or **Staff Portal Roles**) \> \[select role\] > **Permission** \> **Customer**

Site contacts: open the site > **Other Site Contacts / Addresses** \> **Create Contact**

Zone contacts: open the zone > **Contacts** \> **Create Contact**

**Screenshot 19**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941118006935)

The Customer folder before (left) and after (right). Create contact and Edit contact are added, checked by default. Same folder under Staff Portal Roles.

**Screenshot 20**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941118007959)

Site contacts: Create Contact appears only with the Create contact permission. Edit on an existing contact needs Edit contact.

**Screenshot 21**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941129210263)

Zone contacts: the same two permissions apply.

#### Rollout and upgrade

**Rollout method**

Automatic for all. Both permissions are added to every Admin Portal and Staff Portal role, turned on.

**Customer action required**

None — automatic. To limit who can add or change contacts (optional):

1. Go to **Settings** \> **Roles & Security** \> **Roles/Permissions**.
2. Under **Admin Portal Roles** or **Staff Portal Roles**, select the role.
3. On the **Permission** tab, open the **Customer** folder.
4. Uncheck **Create contact**, **Edit contact**, or both.

Create contact and Edit contact are independent. To let a role both add and change contacts, keep both checked.

## Permission to delete Activity Feed records

**Available in:** Web portal · Admin Portal Roles · Live Dashboard (main, site and zone) · All customers

#### Release summary

**Affected modules**

Web portal — Settings > Roles & Security (Admin Portal Roles > Dashboard permission folder); Activity Feed on the Live Dashboard (main dashboard, site and zone level)

**Customer action required**

No — automatic update. The new permission is on by default, so roles that can delete Activity Feed records today keep that ability until an admin turns it off.

#### Overview

Admins can now choose which roles are allowed to delete records from the Activity Feed. Until now, any admin portal user with access to the Activity Feed could permanently delete an event, like a clock-in or clock-out, with a single click. A new permission in the Dashboard folder of Admin Portal Roles controls this. It’s on by default, so nothing changes until an admin turns it off for a role.

**Who benefits most:** Account admins who manage roles, and operations teams who rely on the Activity Feed as the record of what happened on site — who clocked in, who clocked out and when — for audits, payroll and billing questions, or client disputes.

**What drove the change:** Deleting an Activity Feed record is permanent and takes one click, and there was no way to stop a role from doing it. Records could be removed by accident, or by people who shouldn’t be editing the record of events.

#### What's new

**What it does**

Adds a new permission, **Delete Event**, in the **Dashboard** folder of Admin Portal Roles that controls whether a role can delete Activity Feed records:

- **On (default):** users see **Delete** next to each record’s timestamp and can permanently remove it, same as today.
- **Off:** users can still see the Activity Feed but can’t delete records from it. The Delete option is hidden.
- **Everywhere the Activity Feed shows:** the main Live Dashboard, and the Live Dashboard at site and zone level.

**Why it matters**

The Activity Feed is often what admins and clients point to when something is questioned. Admins can now make sure only the right people can remove entries from it, so records don’t disappear by accident or without oversight.

**How to access it**

Turn the permission on or off: **Settings** \> **Roles & Security** \> **Roles/Permissions** \> **Admin Portal Roles** \> \[select role\] > **Permission** \> **Dashboard** \> **Delete Event**

Where the Delete option appears (next to the timestamp on each Activity Feed record):

- **Dashboards** \> **Live Dashboard** \> **Activity Feed**
- **Sites (Client)** \> **Site List** \> \[select site\] > **Security & Patrol** \> **Live Dashboard**
- **Sites (Client)** \> **Site Zones (Groups)** \> \[select zone\] > **Security & Patrol** \> **Live Dashboard**

**Screenshot 22**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941118010647)

Delete sits next to the timestamp on each Activity Feed record. It only shows for roles with the Delete Event permission.

**Screenshot 23**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941129211159)

The same Activity Feed on a site’s Live Dashboard: Sites (Client) > Site List > \[site\] > Security & Patrol > Live Dashboard.

**Screenshot 24**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941129212311)

At zone level: Sites (Client) > Site Zones (Groups) > \[zone\] > Security & Patrol > Live Dashboard. Delete follows the same permission.

**Screenshot 25**

![](https://support.tracktik.com/hc/article_attachments/43941118012183)

The Delete Event permission in the Dashboard folder. On by default; uncheck it to stop a role from deleting Activity Feed records.

#### Rollout and upgrade

**Rollout method**

Automatic for all. The permission is added to Admin Portal Roles and switched on by default.

**Customer action required**

None — automatic. To stop a role from deleting Activity Feed records (optional):

1. Go to **Settings** \> **Roles & Security** \> **Roles/Permissions**.
2. Under **Admin Portal Roles**, select the role.
3. On the **Permission** tab, open the **Dashboard** folder.
4. Uncheck **Delete Event**.
5. Repeat for any other role that shouldn’t delete records.

Changes here also update the matching Policy Permissions; they show on the Policy Permissions tab after a page refresh.
